description: WWII Fletcher-class destroyer ventilation network. Forced-draft supply ventilation only, no filtration, no recirculation. Boiler rooms maintained positive pressure for combustion air. Extreme inter-compartment airflow through open hatches and ladder wells during non-battle conditions.

hvac_zones.description: Superstructure supply ventilation. Unfiltered outside air via mushroom vents and forced-draft blowers. No recirculation.
Forward main deck ventilation. Supply blowers draw outside air through vent trunks. No filtration.
Midships main deck ventilation. Higher ACH in galley for cooking exhaust. Torpedo mount partially open to weather.
Below-deck berthing and mess ventilation. Chronically inadequate in tropical waters. Supply blowers only, no exhaust fans in many compartments.
Forced-draft boiler room ventilation. Massive airflow for combustion supply. Positive pressure maintained. Air drawn from topside and exhausted through stacks.
Engine room forced ventilation. High ACH for heat removal from turbines and reduction gears.
Magazine ventilation for ordnance temperature control. Supply blowers with some temperature monitoring.

cross_zone_links.description: Passive airflow down from superstructure through bridge access ladder. Frequently open during normal operations.
Forward ladder well connecting main deck to second deck berthing. Major cross-contamination pathway.
Midships ladder well. High traffic route between mess/galley and berthing. Significant bidirectional airflow.
Fore-aft airflow through main deck passageway. Narrow corridor acts as duct.
Access trunk from second deck to boiler rooms. Boiler room positive pressure normally pushes air upward.
Access trunk from berthing level to engine rooms.
Cross-connection between boiler and engine rooms through watertight doors (normally open at sea).
Forward magazine ventilation trunk. Ducted supply for ordnance temperature control.
Aft magazine ventilation trunk.
